searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; two left unspent. Six were restricted to a house's own domain and are read as primary through their summaries: villabucci.com once (the estate), monacesca.it twice (the history; the Mirum sheet), umanironchi.com twice (the history; the Cùmaro sheet, with the US history page) and velenosivini.com twice (who we are and Brecciarolo; the Roggio del Filare sheets), counted as six with the house searches shared. Four went to the appellation bodies (the IMT's Castelli di Jesi Riserva disciplinare and Verdicchio page; the IMT's Conero disciplinare and Matelica text; the Regione Marche and MASAF copies of the Rosso Piceno disciplinare; the Consorzio Vini Piceni's page). Six blocked the author's own sources so that a second, independent source would show (Bucci twice, La Monacesca, Fazi Battaglia twice, Umani Ronchi twice, Velenosi). The DOCG search for the Castelli di Jesi is counted with Bucci and the IMT's Conero search, which also gave the Matelica DOCG, with Umani Ronchi. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept in a record marked checked.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the houses' own pages and sheets for their own dates and methods and to the appellation bodies' texts, then to the press and the merchants, with the author's sources blocked where they would only have repeated themselves.

Where the sources corrected the record (Oniverse, the cask months and sizes, the monks' flight, the families' cellar, the takeover of 1968 and the move to Osimo, the Abruzzo estate, the Superiore's ageing and zone, Brecciarolo's first year) the record was set right with its source; where a detail rested on no source the refuter read (vine ages, the building contractor of Ancona, the first export markets, the partner of 2005, the Tenute San Sisto label) it was cut.
Prices on the houses' shops and the merchants' pages, scores, hectares and bottle counts were read and not used.

tested: Ampelio Bucci's death: Sky TG24 and ANSA date it to 21 August 2025, at 89, and Wein.plus and WineNews agree; the record names him with his death and age. His birthplace is Montecarotto in most accounts and in the house's own summary, Senigallia in Wein.plus, and one source gives 1936 for his birth, so no span of years is given.

The sale of 2024: WineNews and Wine Couture give July 2024, to the Oniverse group of the Veronesi family, formerly Calzedonia, with the founder staying on as a consultant; the record's a group of wineries was not what they say.

The house's own page (read through search): the start of the winery dated to 1983 at Ostra Vetere; the vineyards on the hills of Serra de' Conti, Montecarotto and Ostra Vetere, on calcareous and clay soils; large, worn Slavonian oak casks. The founding left empty with the library: the land since the eighteenth century (several merchants), the winery 1983.

The first Villa Bucci of 1983 that could not be labelled Riserva: DoctorWine gives 1983 as the first vintage and a Riserva; Lobenbergs gives a Classico bottled in 1982, a Riserva of 1983 that could not then be labelled so, and the Riserva's official standing only from 1995, the year the IMT gives for the Riserva type of the Matelica DOC. Confirmed.

Vessels and months: two listings give fermentation in steel (spontaneous in one); the casks are 50 and 75 hectolitres in most listings, 50 and 70 in one and 35, 50 and 75 in another; the time in cask 12 to 15 months, 18 months or a year to a year and a half by vintage and source, then about a year in bottle. Changed to what all allow.
Organic farming (certified, by several merchants) confirmed; vine ages of forty to fifty years (several) and fifty to sixty five (one, for 2018) are a figure that moves each year and were cut.

The DOCG: the IMT's disciplinare gives at least 18 months, 6 of them in bottle, from 1 December of the harvest year, and its Verdicchio page the DOCG of 2010; the label words Castelli di Jesi Verdicchio Riserva DOCG Classico on Empson's and Caffetteria Stazione's listings. Confirmed.
The consultant oenologist: a merchant gives nearly thirty years, a writer's own site (not a source) a partnership from 1983 to his death in 2019; the span is unsettled, so for decades.

The house rules: nobody living named (the buyer's family and the writer met and not named); no price, no score, no judging superlative in the record (a source title calling the wine iconic was read and not used); British; no dash. The questions: one key each; the story question's distractors were three towns outside the zone its stem names, now two towns of the zone and Matelica; the explanations teach.

tested: The founding of 1966 by the founder known as Miro, who bought the farm, planted the first vines and built the first cellar, and the first Verdicchio di Matelica of 1973: the house's Italian and English pages and a merchant's page in the results, which names the founder and his son. Confirmed; the library's empty founding is answered by the house.

The monks of Farfa: the house gives around the year 900 and Benedictines from Farfa under the scourge of the Lombards; a merchant's account of the house's history (Liber Group's, by the result list) gives the tenth century and the barbarian invasions. The Lombard kingdom fell in 774, so the record keeps what both allow, monks driven out by invaders, and keeps the house's year as the house's account.

Mirum: the house's sheet (read through search) gives Verdicchio alone from about three hectares at about 400 metres in Contrada Monacesca, grapes left some two weeks past ripeness and picked by hand in the third and fourth weeks of October, a fermentation of twenty days at 20 degrees Celsius in steel, eighteen months in steel and six in glass, and ageing of ten years and more; Callmewine gives Verdicchio alone and at least 18 months in steel on its fine lees. The name for Casimiro, known as Miro, on the house's estate page. Confirmed; no source read ties Chardonnay to Mirum.
The DOCG: the IMT gives the Riserva type of the Matelica DOC from 1995 and the DOCG of February 2010, with at least 18 months of ageing. Confirmed.

The house rules: the founder's son, who runs the house, met and not named; the founder described; no price (a price on the house's page read and not used), no score, no judging superlative, British, no dash. The questions: one key each, four appellations and four years, the explanations teach.

tested: The founding of 1957 at Cupramontana by the founder whose name the house carries: the house's two history pages and Civiltà del bere. Confirmed.

The refounding: the house gives the takeover in 1968 by a man and his son in law, acquiring the brand, and the wine estate reconstituted on 4 January 1968, with the seat and the administration moved to Osimo barely a year later, where the Rosso Conero cellar opened; WineNews, Vinitaly and Millesima give 1968; Civiltà del bere and Fisar give 1959 for the two joining the partnership. No source read calls the father in law a building contractor of Ancona; changed to two entrepreneurs (Diemme Vini's word in the results), the house's date hedged.
The exports of 1973 and Casal di Serra of 1983: the house's timeline. Confirmed; the first markets, Germany and Britain, were not in the refuter's results and are cut.

Cùmaro: the house's sheet gives the vineyard on the edge of Osimo, south east, at about 150 to 200 metres, on very deep chalky loam of Pliocene and Pleistocene marine origin; hand picking in October; destemmed, lightly crushed, fermented in steel at 27 to 29 degrees Celsius for 12 to 14 days on native yeasts, then the malolactic; 12 to 14 months in barriques and 6 to 8 in bottle; the merchants in the results (Ventis, Millesima and Superiore.de among them) agree; the first vintage of 1985 on the house's history. Confirmed. The name from komaros, the strawberry tree, is the house's and stands hedged.

The Conero DOCG: the IMT's disciplinare gives the DOC by decree of 21 July 1967 and the DOCG of 1 September 2004, at least 85 per cent Montepulciano, up to 15 of Sangiovese, and at least two years of ageing from 1 November of the harvest year. Confirmed.

The Abruzzo: the house's leaflet tells of finding an estate near Roseto degli Abruzzi in 2001 and beginning its organic conversion that year; it does not say bought, and Centovie is the name of its Abruzzo wines. Changed.
Pelago a Marche Rosso IGT of Cabernet Sauvignon, Montepulciano and Merlot: the house's page. Confirmed.

The house rules: the son in law, his son and his wife met and not named; no price, no score (scores on the house's pages read and not used), no judging superlative, British, no dash. Osimo lies south of Ancona and inland of the Conero, not between them. The questions: one key each; the story stem is reset to the sources.

changed.now: In 1968 two entrepreneurs, a man and his son in law, took the farm over, kept the founder's name and, by the house's account, refounded it as a wine estate on 4 January; a year later its seat moved to Osimo, south of Ancona and inland of the Conero, where its Rosso Conero cellar opened.
changed.why: No source the refuter read gives the father in law's trade; the house gives the takeover of 1968, the date of 4 January and the move to Osimo a year later where the Rosso Conero cellar opened; Osimo is not between Ancona and the Conero.

tested: The founding of 1984 at Ascoli Piceno by two very young entrepreneurs of the house's name: the house's page and one secondary in the results. Confirmed; both are living and not named.

The company of 2005: the house's page gives Velenosi Srl in 2005, drawing on the experience of a named manager; it does not call him a partner. The estates across the province: the house lists vineyards in four communes of the province and beyond it, in the Abruzzo and the Castelli di Jesi. Both cut from the story.

Brecciarolo from the first harvest of 1984: the house's Brecciarolo page gives a first harvest of 1984, its Il Brecciarolo page a first vintage of 1986. Changed to the house's first years in the 1980s in the story, others and the story question.

Roggio del Filare: the house's sheets for the 2012, 2019 and 2020 vintages give 70 per cent Montepulciano and 30 Sangiovese, about 28 days of maceration in temperature controlled steel, 18 months in new barriques, vineyards at Castorano at about 200 metres; Identità Golose and Tivinum give the first vintage of 1993. Confirmed; two listings give 50 and 100 per cent Montepulciano, so the house's sheet is named.
The Rosso Piceno DOC of 1968: Italian Wikipedia gives the decree of 11 August 1968, and the consortium's page as the author read it agrees. Confirmed.

The Superiore: the Regione Marche's copy of the disciplinare gives at least a year of ageing, release no sooner than 1 November of the year after the harvest and 12 per cent of alcohol, without wood in what the search read; the consortium's page gives thirteen communes and a further period in wood; two secondaries a year in wood; Italian Wikipedia fourteen communes. Changed to what all allow: a smaller zone within the province, at least a year of ageing.

The house rules: the founders, the manager of 2005 and the founders' children met and not named; no price, no score, no judging superlative, British, no dash. The questions: one key each, the story question reset so that its key rests on the house's two pages.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment; the read together agent adds those it judges living to people.json. Ampelio Bucci (died 21 August 2025, at 89) is named with his death. Of unsettled status and described, never named: Casimiro Cifola, La Monacesca's founder of 1966; Gino Umani Ronchi, the founder of 1957; Roberto Bianchi, the father in law of 1968; Antonio Maiocchi, the architect of the amphora; Francesco Angelini, the pharmaceutical industrialist and mayor of Ancona; and the consultant oenologist of Villa Bucci, reported dead in 2019 by one writer's site. Walter Speller and Jancis Robinson, met in Umani Ronchi's press page titles, are already in people.json.
swapNote: The author proposed no swap, and the refuter proposes none. All five picks stand: Bucci and La Monacesca are the library's; Fazi Battaglia, Umani Ronchi and Velenosi are real houses of their appellations, each making the wine the record tells, which their own pages and two or more independent sources bear out. Umani Ronchi also makes Campo San Giorgio, a single vineyard Conero Riserva; Cùmaro, made since 1985 and named on the house's history and leaflet, stays the wine the house is known by.
planNotes: bucci: the note is answered: the label reads Castelli di Jesi Verdicchio Riserva DOCG Classico in the DOCG's years (Empson, Caffetteria Stazione, the IMT's DOCG of 2010), Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC before. The why's family estate is history since the sale of July 2024; a Castelli di Jesi estate would read true.

la-monacesca: the note is answered: Verdicchio alone by the house's sheet and Callmewine, no source tying Chardonnay to Mirum; first made in 1988 (the house's anniversary bottling of 1988 to 2018, as the author read it). The why stands.

fazi-battaglia: the note is answered: the competition of 1953 (the house, Sudfood, Palm Bay, Elle Gourmet), the move to Castelplanio in 1956 (a third account beside the author's two), the Angelini family a few years after 1949 told as history without its year. The why stands.

umani-ronchi: the note is answered: the seat at Osimo from about 1969, a year after the takeover of 1968; the founding of 1957; Cùmaro first made in 1985 and labelled Conero Riserva DOCG. The why's Montepulciano from the slopes of Monte Conero is loose: the vineyard lies on the edge of Osimo, inland of the headland, on the house's sheet.
velenosi: the note is answered: the founding of 1984, the blend of about seven tenths Montepulciano with Sangiovese by the house's sheets, the label Rosso Piceno DOC Superiore. The why stands.
